title: Lothric
snippet: Over time, the ritual of the Linking of the Fire evolved, from a simple temple inside the Royal Gardens to an arena complete with stands, in which Iudex Gundyr's golem would judge those who aspired to become Lords. Countless people throughout the long history of the kingdom came here to take part in the ritual started with Gwyn's sacrifice. All the Fire Keepers who served their purpose of guiding their Champions would be disposed of and dropped inside the Bell Tower of Firelinking Shrine, piling in up in the dozens. Even more were those Champions who tried and failed to link the Flame, becoming the Unkindled, and were buried near the shrine in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard of all those who failed in their task.

title: Age of Dark
snippet: In Ending 2: "The End of Fire", the First Flame is snuffed out, albeit with the Fire Keeper revealing that one day "tiny flames will dance across the darkness", which suggests that the First Flame partially perseveres in the form of embers within the Lords of Cinder of the past. As these Lords will use these embers of the First Flame to exert influence the world, this Age of Dark does not spell finality for the Flame. Alternatively, the player can choose to intervene as the Fire Keeper is about to extinguish the First Flame, by killing her before the cinematic ends. In this ending, the Ashen One instead takes the First Flame for themselves while the final segment of the opening narration is heard: *"Nameless, accursed Undead, unfit even to be cinder...And so it is...that Ash seeketh embers."*

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
The original Lord of Cinder was Gwyn, although more would link the flame and extend the Age of Fire in subsequent eras. Becoming a Lord of Cinder entails a sacrifice, as the Lord is consumed by the First Flame in the process. After Gwyn linked the flame, only his mere husk defended it; with each subsequent linking of the Flame, remnants of each new Lord of Cinder would merge with the previous ones' and strengthen the First Flame's guardian, eventually taking the form of the Soul of Cinder.

Throughout history, countless aspiring Lords were lost attempting to reach the Flame; among those who succeeded, some ultimately lacked the strength to withstand its power, and were burned to ash by the Flame instead of linking it. These individuals came to be known as Unkindled: ill-fated champions who were buried in the Cemetery of Ash, a graveyard which scarcely saw any visitors.

title: Dark Lord
snippet:
Dark Lord -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : **This section of the lore lacks sources and is in need of further expansions and explanations**

The Dark Lords are beings who were meant to become Lords of Cinder, but refused to link the First Flame and extend the Age of Fire, with the specific intent of bringing forth the Age of Dark (also referred to as an "Age of Man"). Dark Lords, while powerful enough to overcome the trials involved in linking the Flame, apparently don't have to inherit a primordial force (such as the First Flame) in order to be deemed worthy of their title. For instance, if the Chosen Undead chooses to become a Dark Lord, abandoning the power of the First Flame, several primordial serpents will nevertheless bow before their new Lord (including both Kaathe and Frampt), even as the Chosen Undead lacks the extraordinary power granted by the Flame.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, the First Flame is so weakened that Lords of Cinder past are resurrected so that the embers of the First Flame inside them serve as fuel for new Linkings. Prince Lothric, who was raised to become the next Lord of Cinder, refused to Link the First Flame, while three of the resurrected Lords of Cinder refused to be used as fuel, leading to resurrection of several Unkindled in the hopes that one of them might slay the fleeting Lords of Cinder and Lothric, and Link the First Flame.

title: Soul of Cinder
snippet:
Soul of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : The Soul of Cinder is the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who have linked themselves to the First Flame through history, becoming Lords of Cinder, and thus is an entity possessing all the abilities of the previous Champions despite just being an empty husk.

It exists as the Flame's last defense inside its Kiln, protecting it from anyone attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength—a role that it has enacted for a very long time, confronting all who entered the Kiln as aspiring Lords.

When tested by an aspiring Champion, the Soul of Cinder would even bring out the remnants of the will and power of the first one to ever link the First Flame: Lord Gwyn himself.

title: Champion Gundyr
snippet: Considering that those who had deceived Gundyr had given him his halberd and charged him with linking the Flame, they must have had a position superior to the king of Lothric but still close to him. This could point to the involvement of Gwyndolin, king of the gods of Irithyll, who had strong ties to Lothric; or the Primordial Serpents, who were already advisors to the royal family. Using Gundyr as a golem to test the strength of future Champions would ensure that those overseeing the linking of the Flame would be guaranteed to find potential Lords with enough power to prolong the Age of Fire.

title: Lore
snippet:
Gwyn, in a final effort to save the Age of Fire, marches with a great deal of his army to the Kiln of the First Flame and sacrifices himself to link with the First Flame, turning the Kiln to ash and incinerating his entire army (making them the Black Knights, who later walk Lordran). The attempt is temporarily successful, however, as the Age of Fire was only extended for at least 1000 years. Gwyn became a Hollow and is from then on known as "Gwyn, Lord of Cinder".

The Four Kings became corrupted and were seduced by evil at some point by Kaathe after Gwyn's fall and their servants turned into Darkwraiths. In an effort to stop them New Londo was flooded with all of its population, trapping the Four Kings with their Darkwraiths in the Abyss.

Soon after, the deities began leaving Lordran. Gwyndolin was the only one of Gwyn's children to stay behind...

title: Aldrich Faithful (item)
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful (item) -  Dark Souls III - item - description 
 description : The holy symbol of the Cathedral of the Deep, and crest of those who see beyond fire to the age of deep waters. Equip to pledge oneself to the Aldrich Faithful covenant.

The faithful ensure that Aldrich, Devourer of Gods, remains undisturbed, by taking the form of loyal spirits and hunting down those who would trespass the ruined cathedral.

Summoning takes place automatically while this is equipped.

title: Gwyn, Lord of Cinder
snippet: Having secured absolute dominion over the world, Gwyn thus began the Age of Fire, a time of prosperity that was characterized by the power of the First Flame and the vision of the Great Lord. Gwyn's clan placed themselves atop the new world order, assuming the role of deities for humans who were their subjects, and Gwyn took the title "god of sunlight". Humans venerated the gods who lived in the city of Anor Londo in the region of Lordran, building an economy and culture around the use of souls, even hunting the descendants of dragons for sport and domesticating some of them. Gwyn left the other two Lords to tend to their own domains: Izalith built her civilization underground where she and her daughters continued to study flame sorcery, and Gravelord Nito remained in the Catacombs to oversee the dead.

title: Timeline
snippet:
The First Flame starts to fade again
Prince Lothric, the designated Lord of Cinder, refuses to link the Flame
Due to the fading of the Flame, time and space begin to stagnate, causing geological disasters and leading the various regions of the world to converge towards Lothric
The previous Lords of Cinder are exhumed from their graves to use the embers of the Flame still within them as fuel for it
Most of the previous Lords of Cinder refuse to contribute to the linking of the Flame and instead prefer to return to their ancient homes
The Unkindled, beings who failed to link the Flame and were reduced to ash without heat, are exhumed from their graves
The Ashen One, one of the many Unkindled, awakens in the Cemetery of Ash, where his peers were buried
The Ashen One, fights their way through the cemetery but finds their way blocked by Iudex Gundyr, an ancient golem tasked with judging the pretender Lords of Cinder

title: Lothric
snippet:
Lothric -  Dark Souls III - location - firelinking_duty 
 firelinking_duty : The tradition of linking the Flame plays a central role in Lothric, testified by the Firelink Shrine's location just outside the city walls, connected to the Royal Gardens. A large number of people throughout the long history of the kingdom came here to take part in the ritual initiated by Lord Gwyn's sacrifice. Those who failed, becoming the Unkindled, were buried near the Shrine in the Cemetery of Ash. Next to the Cemetery was an arena complete with stands, where Iudex Gundyr's golem judged those who aspired to become Lords, testing their strength. The ritual of the linking of the Flame permeated the kingdom at every level up to the royal family, who were obsessed with producing a worthy Champion in their line to preserve their divine mandate as the guardians of the Age of Fire.

title: Bracelet of the Great Lord
snippet:
Bracelet of the Great Lord -  Dark Souls - armor - description 
 description : Bracelet of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, who linked the First Flame.

Lord Gwyn, bearer of the ultimate soul, divided that power among his clan before linking the flame. When he departed, he left only with his greatsword, his garb, and the crown, now bereft of power.

title: Ending (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Ending (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - ending 
 ending : Fulfilling the purpose for which they were brought back to life, the Ashen One links the First Flame and becomes a Lord of Cinder. The Flame connects with their body, slowly setting them ablaze as they sit beside the bonfire.

Although in theory, this leads to a continuation of the once-glorious Age of Fire, this linking of the Flame is but a shadow of the linking as can be performed by the Chosen Undead in *Dark Souls*, echoing the significant weakening of the First Flame, which instead of engulfing the Kiln into an explosive blaze of fire remains weak, barely kindled anew. The world remains dim and covered in ash, with the sun still obscured by a fire-dripping eclipse that resembles the Darksign, further exemplifying that this prolonged Age of Fire will pale when compared to days of old.

title: Timeline
snippet:
The Ashen One is suddenly confronted by Slave Knight Gael, who reached the end of time and devoured the Dark Soul from the pygmy nobles to bring it to the young painter
The Ashen One defeats Gael and obtains the mass of Dark Soul contained in his blood and brinks it back to the young painter in the painted world
The Ashen One, before resuming their journey, learns how the young painter will now be able, using Flame and Darkness, to create a new painted world
The Ashen One, during their journey, obtains an immense amount of souls, reaching the power necessary to link the First Flame
The Ashen One, reaches the First Flame but is confronted by the Soul of Cinder, the manifestation of the previous Lords of Cinder who had linked it and now protect it as its last defense
The Ashen One defeats the Soul of Cinder and gains access to the First Flame

title: Lothric
snippet: In the beginning, the first Fire Keeper had a vision of the end of the Age of Fire and the beginning of an Age of Dark, a barren plane of endless darkness. Acting to ward off an Age of Dark, Ludleth, a student of the art of transposition of Courland, rose to the challenge of becoming a Lord of Cinder, to link the First Flame again and repel the dark vision of the Fire Keeper. Despite his feeble appearance, Ludleth managed to muster the strength necessary to become a Lord, something for which he himself expresses remorse, asking to be forgiven. Ludleth was exiled from his country and collaborated with Lothric to ensure that the Fire Keeper was deprived of her eyes, as well as all future maidens, to prevent them from observing a future without the Flame. The original eyes were sealed away in an enigmatic instance of Firelink Shrine, where the First Flame had all but gone out.

title: Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet:
The prince's decision led the system managing the linking of the Flame to resort to an emergency measure: ringing the bells and awakening the Lords of Cinder of the past from their graves, beings who had previously linked the Flame, to unite their cinders and energize the fading Flame. However, most of the awakened Lords of Cinder refused to sacrifice themselves again and returned to their lands, leaving their thrones at the Firelink Shrine empty.

The ringing of the bells would also awaken the Unkindled, who would hunt down the Lords of Cinder and bring their cinders back to Firelink Shrine. Many of these Unkindled attempted to storm the castle to slay Prince Lothric, but were all killed by the royal guards or by his brother Lorian.

title: Timeline
snippet:
Yhorm, as one of the previous Lords of Cinder, is exhumed from his graves to use the embers of the Flame still within him as fuel for it
Yhorm refuses to contribute to the linking of the Flame once again and instead returns to the Profaned Capital
Yhorm remains on his throne inside the city's ruins to prevent further disastrous uses of the Profaned Flame

title: Kiln of the First Flame (Dark Souls III)
snippet:
Kiln of the First Flame (Dark Souls III) -  Dark Souls III - location - description 
 description : The new version of the familiar place is where lies the First Flame and its guardian, the Soul of Cinder. The location has been greatly altered since its depiction in *Dark Souls*.

Once the player has gathered all of the Lords of Cinder, the Fire Keeper will perform a ritual in which the flames of the Lords will drift to her hands. She will then scatter the flames onto the player, teleporting them to the Kiln of the First Flame.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: Although the system that managed the linking of the First Flame had rung the bells to resurrect the past Lords of Cinder when needed, not all of them have awakened from their resting places. Consequently, once the Flame eventually goes out, at some point these Lords of Cinder from the past will rise again and wander the lands like tiny flames. These beings will possess fragments of the First Flame stored within their bodies in the form of cinders, giving them the powers of the Flame in a world that will be enveloped in Darkness.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet:
Lords of Cinder -  Dark Souls III - character - lore 
 lore : The Lords of Cinder are beings that have linked the First Flame and prolonged the Age of Fire through the centuries. Although many of these champions have followed the sacrifice of Gwyn, Lord of Cinder, not everyone became a Lord of Cinder through heroic deeds or even of free will. One such case is Aldrich, who became a Lord only because he had the strength to become one, despite having obtained such power by devouring an untold number of humans for his own pleasure.

The continuous linking of the Flame eventually culminated in the Soul of Cinder, the deific manifestation of the souls of all those who linked the Flame throughout history. This being, although appearing as an empty husk, inherits the abilities of the Lords of Cinders who have come before. It has long existed as the Flame's last defense inside the Kiln, protecting it from Champions attempting to link it again and acting as the ultimate test of their strength.

title: Cinders of a Lord
snippet:
Cinders of a Lord -  Dark Souls III - item - usage 
 usage : When all cinders have been placed at their respective thrones in Firelink Shrine, the player gains access to the Kiln of the First Flame, where they can confront the Soul of Cinder.

title: Ashen One
snippet: ***The End of Fire**: If the Ashen One gave the Eyes of a Fire Keeper to the Fire Keeper, they may summon her upon defeating the Soul of Cinder. The Fire Keeper will take the First Flame into her hands. She states that the fire quickly fades and that dark will soon settle, but predicts that one day, tiny flames will dance across the darkness, like embers linked by lords past, suggesting that the other Lords of Cinder of the past will one day rise and wander through the darkness with their own fragments of the First Flame. As the absolute darkness settles upon the world, the Fire Keeper asks if the Ashen One can still hear her.

title: Ludleth of Courland
snippet: When the link of fire was threatened, the Lords of Cinder would be exhumed from their graves to once again serve as kindling for the First Flame. Ludleth was among those resurrected; though unlike the other three Lords, he accepted the call, and took up his throne at Firelink Shrine to await his fate.

title: Unkindled
snippet:
Unkindled -  Dark Souls III - storyline - background 
 background : To "link the First Flame" is to reach it, be powerful enough to withstand its power, and rekindle the flame anew. The Unkindled were strong enough to overcome the challenges of reaching the Kiln of the First Flame, but lacked the strength needed to withstand the power of the Flame: the primordial Fire burned them to ash, not fueled enough to properly spark anew. These failed champions' remains were entombed in the Cemetery of Ash.

title: Lorian, Elder Prince and Lothric, Younger Prince
snippet: Lothric, the younger prince, was the destined Lord of Cinder, who would sacrifice himself as fuel for the First Flame to uphold the Age of Fire. The prince, born a sickly, frail child, was nevertheless viewed as the "last hope of his line", the culmination of generations of Lothric rulers obsessed with producing worthy Champions for the Flame. For the anticipated journey of the young prince to the Kiln of the First Flame, a platinum sword was crafted and blessed with strong magic by the High Priestess, long before he was ready to fulfill his destiny. Oceiros created extensive propaganda around Lothric, not only giving him the name of the kingdom, but also building statues that depicted him with his sacred sword ready to complete his task, as well as preparing his throne at the Firelink Shrine in advance.

title: First Flame
snippet: Desperate to ensure that their Age of Fire continued, and afraid of the coming Dark, the Lords did everything they could to keep the First Flame lit. Gwyn's clan linked the sacred bonfires that were tied to the Flame to humanity, and shepherded the humans who worshipped them to kindle the flames. The Witch of Izalith attempted to use her own powerful soul to create a new First Flame, but this attempt failed, instead creating the perverse Flame of Chaos and transforming the Witch into the Bed of Chaos, which would go on to birth the race of Demons.

title: Farron Follower
snippet: At some point, the Abyss Watchers would become Lords of Cinder, sacrificing their shared power in the wolf blood to link the fading First Flame. With the wolf blood dried up, the Undead Legion's numbers rapidly dwindled. Over time, the land of Farron, where the bodies of countless warriors of the past were buried, fell into ruin and became a rotten and poisonous forest, and the remaining acolytes of the Undead Legion were corrupted, their descendants becoming Ghrus. The Farron Followers lost their role and reason to exist along with their home, and went hollow, surviving as a wandering pack of Hollows. They drifted aimlessly until they were eventually drawn into the Painted World of Ariandel, where they were welcomed by the other forlorn souls and found refuge.

title: Firelink Armor
snippet:
Firelink Armor -  Dark Souls III - armor - description 
 description : Armor of the Soul of Cinder, a deific manifestation of the Lords of Cinder, who linked the First Flame.

It resembles a knight's armor, but bears hideous burns and contortions, taking the shape of a deathly ribcage.

It exists as a symbol of the great Lords and the noble act of linking the fire, though it is no more than an empty husk.

title: Lothric
snippet:
The relations between the two realms soon blossomed into an alliance, formalized by the incorporation of the sword of Lothric, a symbol of that realm, into the insignia of the Blades of the Darkmoon, the predecessors of the Blue Sentinels and the Way of Blue. In practice, the unification of cultural and religious symbols of the kingdoms allowed the usage of transport demons by those bearing the banner of Lothric.

Now in possession of the knowledge provided by the primordial serpents and the ancient gods of Anor Londo, the kingdom of Lothric developed its role in the linking of the Flame, building the Firelink Shrine just outside the city walls, neighbouring the Royal Gardens, in order to guarantee safe and regulated passage to the Kiln of the First Flame. The shrine would once again accept Fire Keepers who assisted Champions that aspired to link the Flame, drawing out the strength of the souls they acquired to aid them in their journey.

title: Yhorm the Giant
snippet:
Due to a curse triggered by the four female relatives of an unknown oracle, which also turned them into careless greedy creatures, the Profaned Flame was unleashed, a flame that never goes out. Yhorm became a Lord of Cinder to put the Profaned Flame to rest, even as many spoke insincerely of his role. However, after he became a Lord of Cinder, the hellish flame fell out of the sky and destroyed the city, yet consuming naught but human flesh, incinerating the human inhabitants. The flame, despite deriving from Dark and the Abyss, actively sought to harm humanity.

Before linking the First Flame, he gave his other Storm Ruler to Siegward, who promised to end Yhorm's suffering if he ever returned to life.

title: Lords of Cinder
snippet: By the events of *Dark Souls III*, Prince Lothric, who was raised to become a Lord of Cinder, refused to link the First Flame. This led to Lords of Cinder from the past being exhumed from their graves: these Lords were meant to sacrifice themselves to the Flame once again, using what little embers remained within themselves as kindling. However, most of these Lords refused the call, and instead settled back into their domains. To prevent the First Flame from dying out, the Unkindled would then be resurrected as a last resort; these Champions were bound to seek the absconded Lords of Cinder, and forcefully bring them back—in the form of their cinders—to their empty thrones at Firelink Shrine. Once all five Lords "sat" their thrones, an Unkindled Champion would be bestowed the embers of these Lords, and sent to the Kiln of the First Flame to overcome the final challenge and link the Flame.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - benefits 
 benefits : Like the Watchdogs of Farron, Aldrich Faithful will be called upon to defend Aldrich's territory from trespassers; any player who has Host of Embers status will be subject to invasion. This area is defined as anywhere from the courtyard upon exiting Pontiff Sulyvahn's arena, up until the rotating stairway leading up to Anor Londo. Aldrich Faithful can pursue trespassers up into the cathedral itself, but will not be summoned for trespassers who have already reached the upper level bonfire.

Defeating the Host of Embers will reward all present Aldrich Faithful with Human Dregs, which can be offered to Archdeacon McDonnell to deepen their allegiance to the covenant.

title: Aldrich Faithful
snippet:
Aldrich Faithful -  Dark Souls III - mechanic - location 
 location : The Aldrich Faithful covenant can be found in the lower plane of Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

From the Pontiff Sulyvahn bonfire, proceed onward and make way to the other side of the large courtyard with several dead Giant Slaves. Upon entering the main building on the opposite side, hit the wall on the left to reveal an illusory wall concealing the main access to the covenant.

Climb down the large ladder to reach a big, flooded hall. There are two Sulyvahn's Beasts lying in wait once reaching this area, one on the left and one further ahead on the right.

In one corner of the room lie the remains of Archdeacon McDonnell. Interacting with him allows access into the covenant.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: As the First Flame continued to fade and Prince Lothric refused to link it, the Lords of Cinder of the past were exhumed from their graves to once again be used as fuel. However, most Lords refused the call to action, with Aldrich denouncing his throne based on an epiphany: that an Age of Deep would soon be cast upon the world. The Cathedral had by then become a shrine to unspeakable horrors, to all repulsive rejects that sought a cure in its cleansing waters. Within the Cathedral—in McDonnell's sorceries, and their taboo miracles— Aldrich observed a stagnation that seemed inherent to the world, belike rotten remains which find their way down into a dark, deep seabed. Following these ruminations on the nature of existence, Aldrich concluded that an Age of Deep was what followed the waning Age of Fire. He understood that all things would stagnate into the Deep, including the representatives of the old world order; he also understood that he was in a position where he could help usher

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
In the soul of Aldrich, there is a distinct lighter portion inside the soul that is not present in other deep soul; it is probably what's left of Gwyndolin's soul.
The comic *Dark Souls: The Breath of Andolus* features a scryer named Aldrich as the deuteragonist, potentially as a reference to him, despite them not being the same character. Alternatively, it may have been Aldrich long in the past, given he begins to adopt Aldrich's characteristics, such as cannibalism. While he claims to have been forced into it, the scryer Aldrich is later revealed to be a two faced schemer.
The music played during his fight is a more sinister and macabre arrangement of Gwyndolin's theme from the first game, as he uses the body of the god to defend himself, there are also elements from Nito's theme that are played in the first phase as displayed by the sinister chants and piano notes that are also prevalent in Nito's theme.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - description 
 description : Aldrich is an expansive sludge of maggot-ridden rotten flesh, humanity dregs, and his own bones as well as those of the victims he has consumed.

By the time the player reaches him, he will be inert and spread across the floor, using the weapons and malformed body of Gwyndolin to interact with his environment and perform attacks.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: He gathered an army of deacons, who cast off their red robes and crowns—symbolic of their clerical duties— for new dark-blue ones and swore fealty as Aldrich Faithful, their venerance of the Deep finally codified under Aldrich's banner. He then marched on Irithyll, home to the old gods of Anor Londo and the residence of Chief Deity Gwyndolin. Likely forcing his way through the city's magical barrier, he would confront the forces of Pontiff Sulyvahn, who had no intention of relinquishing his power and authority over the city. From the battle that ensued, Aldrich emerged victorious, slaughtering Sulyvahn's troops and forcing him into capitulation. Seemingly, the two eventually struck a deal: the Pontiff would maintain some control over lower Irithyll; in exchange, Aldrich would be granted access to Gwyndolin, who was imprisoned by the Pontiff within the old Cathedral of Anor Londo.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: At his new posting at the Cathedral, Aldrich was provided a steady flow of sustenance in the form of the Road of Sacrifices. The Cathedral would dispatch Evangelists to establish missions and gain influence at the Undead Settlement; these preachers would tell stories of enlightenment to the cursed Undead, who were shipped off en masse to become feed to Aldrich's gluttony. At some point, he would desire for others to share in the elation of devouring men; to this end he fashioned warped magic rings that allowed one to feel the same depraved sensations as the repulsive maneater. The bearers of these rings underwent a mutation similar to his, transforming into bestial creatures with stomachs filled with the remains of their meals and infused with the power of the Deep.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: Continuing to gorge himself on humans and devouring their very essence, Aldrich eventually attained an extraordinary amount of power, and with it the qualifications to become a Champion to link the First Flame. As the Flame waned, Aldrich was prepared to become a Lord of Cinder just for his strength, without any consideration for his morality or how he acquired his power. Now left to indulge in his every perversion so that he could one day link the Flame, Aldrich was even allowed to eat children, some of them his own. Aldrich, despite his unbridled hedonism, still decided to follow his ideals on the Age of Fire as a cleric and, when the time came, he sacrificed himself on the Flame to prolong its life.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - theories 
 theories : It is possible to theorize that the many children that Aldrich had when he was trapped inside the Cathedral of the Deep were the results of repeated violence on Rosaria, Mother of Rebirth. Rosaria's room is covered with cradles and Aldrich was already known for having had multiple children, of whom Anri and Horace are the only survivors. Additionally, Rosaria's soul has a broken and twisted appearance, and Ringfinger Leonhard talks about how his goddess's body has been violated.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
When he rears up and aims his bow, he will launch an expanding wave of highly damaging arrows in front of him, allowing you to circle behind him and get hits in.

Throughout the course of the battle, Aldrich will be constantly summoning small homing projectiles. Each one of these, on its own, only deals a small amount of damage and the player may even opt to sustain a few of them in exchange of inflicting some damage to the boss. However, if they are caught by the full attack, they will sustain heavy damage, which may even kill them in a single barrage.

Aldrich is most vulnerable on his tail, which provides an area where the player may attack without risking themselves too much from being in the staff's range.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - strategy 
 strategy : At the beginning of the fight, charge at Aldrich to avoid his hard-hitting soul spear. Get behind him and focus your attacks on his tail. This leaves him with nothing to do but swing his two slow, devastating melee attacks or teleport across the room (usually, adjacent to where he teleported from).

At about 55%-60% health, he will teleport and come back up, buffed with fire. His arrows also go from going forward to following a specific player. If the arrows following the player catch up to them, then that player will most likely go down quick. Blue Bug and Red Bug Pellets are recommended for this fight.

Casting the sorcery Twisted Wall of Light can negate Aldrich's ranged attacks, including his arrow barrage in the second phase, allowing one to wait out the attack by casting repeatedly.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: However, although the monstrous man-eater had done his duty and was no longer active, the effect of his stay in the Cathedral had become profound. Aldrich, through devouring humans and their Dark Souls, had accumulated an immense amount of darkness that remained in his body to ferment and degenerate, becoming dark dregs, a darkness beyond any natural limit. The Cathedral's sacred and peaceful body of water that served for purification had consequently been infected, continuing to accumulate and stagnate filth to the point of becoming the "Deep", an abyssal sea of rotten darkness. This dark pool became a cradle of repulsive life, which began to spawn ravenous insects and maggots that infested the corpses buried around the church and brought them back to life. snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - lead 
 lead : , also known as , is a boss and one of the five Lords of Cinder encountered by the Ashen One in *Dark Souls III*.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: With Pontiff Sulyvahn's rise to power in Irithyll, as well as his complete domination of the Way of White faith within the city, Aldrich's depraved habit became likely to draw unwanted attention to the Pontiff's new "holy" regime. In response, Pontiff Sulyvahn seems to have exiled Aldrich to the Cathedral of the Deep, which specialized in rituals of purification from "stagnant darkness", in hopes that the sacred and serene waters of the Cathedral would contain Aldrich's dark habit. The Pontiff also gave one of his small dolls to Aldrich, in the event that he recovered to a point where he could return home.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
While the attacks of Gwyndolin were light blue energy that dealt magic damage in the first game, Aldrich uses variations of the same attacks with purple energy that dealt dark damage.
Innumerable bones and large amounts of sludge can be seen on the floor of the arena, similar in appearance to Aldrich himself, and possibly being actually part of his body. If this is the case, then, Aldrich insists on attacks by exerting his will over the body of Gwyndolin, instead of simply devouring the player.
The sludge and bones remain after Aldrich dies, though they are inert, making him and Archdeacon Royce the only two bosses to leave behind physical remains.
His melee attacks, during his first phase, closely resemble those of Nito.
Aldrich's staff uses a Dark Miracle version of Nito's Gravelord Sword and in the deleted files Aldrich was able to do the Gravelord Sword Dance miracle.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
With Pontiff Sulyvahn relinquishing Gwyndolin, the Saint of the Deep was triumphant, taking up residence in the old Cathedral and beginning to feast on the old god. He would fall into a deep slumber in the process of consuming Gwyndolin, during which he would dream and perceive the form of a young, pale girl in hiding. The Aldrich Faithful guarded the old Cathedral to ward off any intrusion on Aldrich's slumber, with the ancient Silver Knights unwittingly aiding the consumption of their former master.

When the Ashen One seeking the Lords of Cinder arrives at Irithyll to slay Aldrich in their quest, he awakens to defend himself, puppeteering Gwyndolin's magic and body, as well as using a miracle developed from his dreams.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - lore 
 lore : Aldrich was once a cleric of the Way of White originating from Irithyll of the Boreal Valley, implying that he may have been a descendant of the gods of Anor Londo. Despite his status as a man of faith serving the gods, he was actually a depraved cleric who took pleasure in devouring humans and indulging in their last screams. For the cleric, eating people became a routine, keeping it up so long that his own body bloated, becoming melted sludge.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich is most vulnerable on his tail, which provides an area where the player may attack without risking themselves too much from being in the staff's range.

Upon receiving some damage, Aldrich will raise his staff and create a big vortex on the ground in front of him, plunging inside to escape from punishment. This vortex is heavily damaging and the player would be wise in not attacking the boss too many times in a row, preparing instead to move away when it is cast. Aldrich will emerge a moment later on the other side of the hall, as far away from the player as possible, trying to buy some time to cast more spells.

Once Aldrich has lost about 40% of his health, he will buff his scythe with fire. At this point, every time he emerges from the ground, he will deal damage to nearby players while a much greater amount of homing projectiles spawn with him as he rises.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - location 
 location : Aldrich is found in Anor Londo in the same cathedral hall where Ornstein and Smough were fought in *Dark Souls.*

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich's staff uses a Dark Miracle version of Nito's Gravelord Sword and in the deleted files Aldrich was able to do the Gravelord Sword Dance miracle.
As he is an amalgamation of corpses just like Nito and the Rotten, and his overall resemblance to Nito, it could be theorized that Aldrich is the new gravelord or that he found the soul of the old dead one, which allowed him to pursue his cannibalistic habits further.
In original his name writing like エルドリッチ which can be translated as Eldritch, that means “mystic, unnatural, frightening”, with an association with terror or horror that cannot be comprehended by the human mind. The whole theme of The Deep and Age of Deep Sea may be inspired by such horrors.
In the soul of Aldrich, there is a distinct lighter portion inside the soul that is not present in other deep soul; it is probably what's left of Gwyndolin's soul.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
He will also use a replica of the Lifehunt Scythe, starting a large windup before spinning twice in a full circle, and stealing health with each target that it connects to. This attack is telegraphed, and one can see the miracle generating on his staff, but it can often be confused for another standard swing.

His most devastating attack is, without a doubt, is taking out Gwyndolin's bow and shooting toward the sky, making an extensive barrage of arrows rain over the player and follow them for a considerable amount of time. He telegraphs this attack by suddenly stopping and erecting his upper body, while a white flash of light emanates from him. Being caught under the rain of arrows, practically means instant death. As soon as this attack is detected, the player is advised to completely disengage from battle and start running throughout the room with no specific direction.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: Age of Fire. He understood that all things would stagnate into the Deep, including the representatives of the old world order; he also understood that he was in a position where he could help usher in the new Age. Thus he set out to devour the old gods himself, stagnating these obsolete forces into the Deep Sea.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - fight_overview 
 fight_overview : The encounter begins with Aldrich standing on the far end of the room, imbuing his staff with magic and wielding it menacingly while he prepares for battle. He specializes in ranged combat, doing so by casting diverse dangerous magical spells. Conversely, his close combat abilities become heavily compromised due to his sluggish mobility and tendency to miss hits with his weapon. His substandard melee abilities should not be underestimated, however, because what he lacks in accuracy, he more than makes it up in damage-dealing potential.

When he rears up and aims his bow, he will launch an expanding wave of highly damaging arrows in front of him, allowing you to circle behind him and get hits in.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet:
Aldrich, Devourer of Gods -  Dark Souls III - boss - trivia 
 trivia : Aldrich's throne in Firelink Shrine refers to him as "Saint Aldrich of the Deep".
Before eating Gwyndolin, Aldrich imposed on himself a practice of asceticism (苦行), that is, he refrained from eating humans before he could devour the god.
During the fight, as well as when the boss is passive, shrieks and moans of pain can be heard coming from Gwyndolin. As Aldrich was half-way through consuming Gwyndolin and had used the God's body to defend himself, this disturbingly implies that Gwyndolin was still alive (albeit barely) and in a semi-conscious state of being continuously devoured by Aldrich, even during the fight.
While the attacks of Gwyndolin were light blue energy that dealt magic damage in the first game, Aldrich uses variations of the same attacks with purple energy that dealt dark damage.

title: Aldrich, Devourer of Gods
snippet: At one point, Sulyvahn sent McDonnell, an Archdeacon from Irithyll that was a sorcerer despite being a high-ranking cleric, to help the deacons of the Cathedral. McDonnell shared his sorceries with the priests of the Cathedral, who in turn became sorcerers, turning their holy candles into sorcery staves and blades, better equipped to face the abominations of the Deep. However McDonnell would soon find delight in the stagnant souls of the Deep, believing the place to be the "bottom of the world". Over time the deacons themselves, despite their faith and holy flame, began to succumb to the power of the Deep. They began to add dark stories about the Deep to the holy scriptures intended to grant them divine protection, corrupting these holy tales into profanity. McDonnell realized that the rotten darkness of the Deep could become an incredible new power, and by studying it, he created sorceries that manipulated the dark soul dregs, then imparted them to Archdeacon Royce and his deacons.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
The Ashen One may also rescue Cornyx of the Great Swamp, a master of pyromancy who will offer his teachings to the Ashen One. Upon finding the church in the center of the settlement, the Ashen One encounters Eygon of Carim, a disdainful knight of Carim. If the Ashen One purchases a key from the handmaiden, they may free Eygon's ward, a blind nun by the name of Irina, who will offer to tell the Ashen One stories of miracles. After freeing her, Eygon will offer an alliance to the Ashen One, for as long as Irina's safety is guaranteed.

Inside the church, the Ashen One encounters Siegward of Catarina, a Catarina knight who is perplexed by a lift that will only take him down, rather than up where he wishes to speak to the Giant. If the Ashen One solves the riddle of the lift, they may make peace with the Giant, who will offer his help.

Once through the settlement, the Ashen One makes it to the Road of Sacrifices, where offerings were once transported to Aldrich, Saint of the Deep.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - lead 
 lead : The **Ashen One,** also referred to as the **Champion of Ash** or **the Unkindled One,** is the playable character and the protagonist of *Dark Souls III*.

The title of Ashen One is given to the player by the Fire Keeper of Firelink Shrine. The Ashen One is an Unkindled, an Undead who failed to link the First Flame and became ash, who has been raised from their grave, and is tasked with a journey to defeat four Lords of Cinder and return them to their thrones, since the link of the Flame is threatened and the Lords refuse to serve as its fuel once again.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - irithyll_and_anor_londo_dark_souls_iii_anor_londo 
 irithyll_and_anor_londo_dark_souls_iii_anor_londo : On the surface, the Ashen One fights their way to the grand church in Irithyll where they find Pontiff Sulyvahn. Killing Sulyvahn opens the way to Anor Londo, fabled city of the gods, where Aldrich awaits. Aldrich, having lost interest in the flame and having instead turned towards the Dark, sought out Anor Londo to devour the gods themselves. He found and devoured Dark Sun Gwyndolin in Anor Londo, who had been "stricken by illness" and had retreated to the Anor Londo Cathedral, only to be imprisoned by the Pontiff to be fed to Aldrich. Fighting their way past the archers protecting the city, the Ashen One finds Aldrich using Gwyndolin as a puppet of sorts, and kills him, acquiring his ashes to be delivered to his throne.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - farron_keep 
 farron_keep : Returning to the Crucifixion Woods and progressing towards Farron Keep, the Ashen One finds a massive swamp, the corrupted remnants of the once-vibrant Royal Wood. In order to make their way to the Abyss Watchers, the Ashen One must extinguish three flames, per the ceremony of admission into the Undead Legion. After doing so, the path to the Keep opens, allowing the Ashen One to face the Abyss Watchers.

The Abyss Watchers, reduced to fighting amongst themselves, are defeated by the Ashen One, who claims their ashes in order to restore them to their throne in Firelink Shrine. Killing the Watchers opens the way to the Catacombs of Carthus, an underground tomb filled with skeletal warriors.

title: Ashen One
snippet: Within the city, the Ashen One may encounter Shira, Knight of Filianore, who asks the Ashen One to put down Midir, a mighty dragon who once served the Gods, but who has now been consumed by the Dark. Fighting their way through the city, the Ashen One finds Midir and sends him hurtling down a chasm. Chasing Midir to his lair, the Ashen One may fulfill Shira's request and fight him to the death. In the Church of Filianore, the Ashen One finds Judicator Argo who bars the way to Filianore. He will summon Halflight, Spear of the Church to fight the Ashen One.

 epilogue : ***Link the Fire**: In this ending, the Ashen One attempts to do as all the other lords had done before them and link the fire. The Ashen One stretches out a hand and begins to burn, but unlike in the past, the fire is not rekindled. Instead, the Ashen One merely sits beside the flame, unable to prolong its life, as the sun remains a Darksign.

title: Ashen One

If the Ashen One chooses to ignore Friede and explores the Painted World, they may fight the Champion's Gravetender and Gravetender Greatwolf, which allows the Ashen One to participate in the Undead Match. Deeper inside the painting, the Ashen One finds the Painter, Slave Knight Gael's aforementioned Lady, who has been imprisoned by Friede and Vilhelm in order to prevent her from painting the next world. If the Ashen One opens the way to the inner sanctum hiding Father Ariandel, Friede will confront them and fight to preserve the painting. After a long battle, the Ashen One defeats Friede and Ariandel, prompting the Painted World to begin burning and dooming it to destruction.

The Painter informs the Ashen One that she has sent Gael to find the Dark Soul, which she will use for her next painting.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
After killing Oceiros, the Ashen One acquires the means to access two more optional areas. One is a gesture that will allow passage to Archdragon Peak, and the other is a secret path to the Untended Graves, a dark version of Firelink Shrine. Here the Ashen One finds Champion Gundyr, and behind him an abandoned Firelink Shrine home only to a Shrine Handmaiden. Here the Ashen One can find the Eyes of a Fire Keeper which if presented to the Firekeeper will allow her to see a dark vision of the future that the Ashen One may choose to fulfill.

In Archdragon Peak, the Ashen One can face the Ancient Wyvern and The Nameless King, once known as Lord Gwyn's Firstborn, the old God of War who aligned himself with the Ancient Dragons.

title: Ashen One
snippet: After defeating Halflight, the path to Filianore is open. Filianore lies sleeping while clutching a broken egg-like object. If the Ashen One touches the object, it will shatter into pieces and Filianore will wake, upon which a blinding light emanates from the shards of the object and envelopes the chamber. The Ashen One opens their eyes to find that the Ringed City is now a lifeless desert, and Filianore an emaciated corpse. Leaving her room, the Ashen One comes upon a fleeing Pygmy. Investigating the scene closer, they find Gael consuming the remains of a Pygmy Lord in order to gain their Dark Soul. He proceeds to attack the Ashen One in order to gain their piece of the Dark Soul.

title: Ashen One

Ashen One -  Dark Souls III - character - cemetery_of_ash 
 cemetery_of_ash : At some point in time, the Ashen One attempted to link the fire. They were not powerful enough and were instead burnt to ash by the flames. Some time later, the Ashen One was awakened by the toll of the bells in the Cemetery of Ash, signifying that the link of fire was threatened. The Ashen One emerges from their grave and sets out to leave their tomb. Finding the Coiled Sword lodged inside Iudex Gundyr, the Ashen One pulls it out, awakening Gundyr and beginning a fight. Halfway through, Gundyr is seemingly consumed by the Pus of Man, but the Ashen One defeats him and finds Firelink Shrine.

title: Ashen One

snippet:

 catacombs_of_carthus : Progressing through the trap-ridden Catacombs, the Ashen One eventually finds a rickety drawbridge that will lead them to Irithyll of the Boreal Valley. Should the Ashen One choose to descend the fallen drawbridge, they may find the Smouldering Lake, ruled by the Old Demon King and home to various demons and a great slithering worm.

Across the bridge, the Ashen One finds a strange goblet that pulls them into the Abyss. Here they encounter High Lord Wolnir, who attacks the Ashen One. By destroying his enchanted bracelets, Wolnir loses his grip and falls into the Abyss, allowing the Ashen One to return to the regular world, where the path to Irithyll, a frozen city guarded by an impenetrable barrier and ruled by Pontiff Sulyvahn in the name of Aldrich, is now open.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
Deep within the Cathedral, the Ashen One encounters the Deacons of the Deep guarding Aldrich's tomb. After defeating them, the Ashen One finds that Aldrich has left the cathedral, finding instead a doll that will allow the Ashen One to enter Irithyll of the Boreal Valley.

After returning to Firelink Shrine, the Ashen One again encounters Anri and Horace, who tell the Ashen One that Aldrich supposedly hails from Irithyll and that he may have returned home. They will also find Sirris of the Sunless Realms, who shows little interest in the Ashen One, unless they provide the Handmaiden with a certain ash, prompting Sirris to offer the Ashen One her sign.

snippet: The Ashen One defeats Gael, and gains the Blood of the Dark Soul. title: Ashen One
snippet: At this point in the game, Yoel of Londor will die. If the Ashen One has allowed him to draw out their true strength a sufficient number of times, Yoel will be replaced by Yuria of Londor, who attempts to sway the Ashen One into usurping the First Flame and becoming the Lord of Hollows.

title: Ashen One
snippet:
***Ash Seeketh Embers**: If the Ashen One gave the Eyes of a Fire Keeper to the Fire Keeper, they may summon her upon defeating the Soul of Cinder. The Fire Keeper will take the First Flame into her hands. Before the flames fade, the Ashen One may strike her down. The Ashen One steps over the limp body of the Fire Keeper and takes the First Flame into their own hands. Kneeling, the Ashen One raises the flame, offering it to the Darksign Sun.
***The Usurpation of Fire**: If the Ashen One allowed Yoel to draw out their true strength a sufficient amount of times through the Dark Sigil, followed Yuria's instructions and "married" Anri, the Ashen One may, instead of linking the fire, absorb it into themselves. The Ashen One collapses from the strain and awakens before a Darksign Sun turned white, and also finds Yuria, Anri, and an army of hollows greeting them as their Lord and praying for the Ashen One to make Londor whole.

 road_of_sacrifices_and_crucifixion_woods : Following the road leads the Ashen One to the Crucifixion Woods, where they encounter Anri of Astora and their companion Horace the Hushed. Anri seeks Aldrich, and thinks to find him in the Cathedral of the Deep. They offer their help to the Ashen One, should the Ashen One need it. Here the Ashen One may also find Orbeck of Vinheim, a sorcerer who will offer to share his knowledge if the Ashen One brings him magic scrolls.

Making their way through the Crucifixion Woods leads the Ashen One to a crossroads. One path leads to Farron Keep, home of the Abyss Watchers, whereas the other one, guarded by one of the Crystal Sages, leads to the Cathedral of the Deep, home of Aldrich.

 the_painted_world_of_ariandel : Within the Cathedral of the Deep the Ashen One can encounter Slave Knight Gael, a Slave Knight who seeks unkindled ash to aid his Lady. Gael presents the Ashen One with a fragment of the Painted World of Ariandel, which sucks the Ashen One in. Within the painting, the Ashen One encounters Sister Friede and her loyal knight Sir Vilhelm. Friede is an advisor to Ariandel, the painting's creator, and convinced him to allow the painting to rot rather than allow it to be destroyed and replaced by a new one, despite the wishes of many of the painting's denizens. Friede bids the Ashen One to leave, telling them that they do not belong in the Painted World.

title: Ashen One

 undead_settlement : Arriving in the Undead Settlement, the Ashen One finds Yoel of Londor praying for death at a ledge. Upon encountering the Ashen One, Yoel offers his services, providing rudimentary sorceries and offering to draw out the Ashen One's "true strength", not telling them that doing so will burden the Ashen One with the Dark Sigil which will make them hollow upon death.

Inside the Settlement, the Ashen One is accosted by the inhabitants of the town and pelted with massive arrows by a Giant atop a tower. After fighting and killing the Curse-rotted Greatwood, the Ashen One will find a Transposing Kiln that will allow Ludleth to provide great spells and weapons from the souls of powerful creatures.

 grand_archives_and_prince_lothric : Progressing through Lothric Castle will bring the Ashen One face to face with a Dragonslayer Armour controlled by a Pilgrim Butterfly. Defeating the armour opens the way to the Grand Archives, home to ancient knowledge.

The Ashen One fights their way through the Archives, and find themselves close to the location of Prince Lothric, who hides at the very top of the castle. Lothric has no intention of returning as a Lord of Cinder however, preferring to watch the world end from afar with his brother Lorian. The brothers attack the Ashen One, who slays them both, and claims Lothric's ashes.

 trivia : The Ashen One, as depicted in promotional material, is a Knight.

 high_wall_of_lothric : The Ashen One then progresses through the High Wall of Lothric, now home to mindless hollow soldiers, knights, and a fire-breathing wyvern. Emma provides them with a banner that will allow them safe passage to the Undead Settlement, but warns them that their path is guarded by Vordt of the Boreal Valley. Emma also gives the opportunity to join the Way of Blue covenant. Also in the High Wall is Greirat of the Undead Settlement, a thief that will swear himself to the Ashen One if they rescue him from his cell and promises to look for a woman named Loretta in the Undead Settlement.

After finding and defeating Vordt, the Ashen One raises the banner on a ledge, and is transported by Batwing Demons to the Undead Settlement, a dilapidated town inhabited by hollows.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:

 quelaag_s_domain_bell : The other Bell is significantly harder to reach. The Chosen Undead must first head downward and find their way into Blighttown, a multileveled and dangerous labyrinth. At the very bottom of Blighttown, the player will traverse a poison swamp leading to a half-demon's lair known as Quelaag's Domain. It is here that the player must defeat Chaos Witch Quelaag in order to progress to the Bell of Awakening.

Upon ringing the second Bell, a short cutscene plays showing the gatekeeper Giant hearing the call and pulling the chains to lift up the portcullis, bearing passage to Sen's Fortress. It is at this point that Kingseeker Frampt appears in Firelink Shrine, and instructs the player that his new task is to secure the Lordvessel, proving that the player is in fact, the Chosen Undead.

title: Bells of Awakening
snippet:
Bells of Awakening -  Dark Souls - mechanic - lead 
 lead : The **Bells of Awakening** are a storyline concept, as well as two locations, in *Dark Souls*.

They are the first destinations hinted at for the Chosen Undead after they have escaped the Undead Asylum into Lordran. The two Bells are part of a prophecy devised by the Gods of Anor Londo to help bring about an Undead to link the First Flame. The two Bells are respectively located past the Bell Gargoyles atop the Undead Parish, and past Queelag past the swamp at the bottom of Blighttown. Both Bells must be rung by activating levers near them to progress, opening the way to Sen's Fortress.
